Judge Alston proceeded to show that the negro is dependent upon the white man for protection—that the law offers protection to all alike—that only the coward would deprive the weak or any right. Some days ago Judge A. H. Alston, Circuit Judge at large, found it his duty to address a special grand jury summoned in St. Clair County to consider the acts of a mob there. In the course of his address to the grand jury, he made these remarks:

The negro ran away and was pursued by a crowd of thirty or more white men. The sheriff was present and urged the parties to desist, but his remonstrations were met with oaths and the crowd continued to pursue the negro and were threatening to do violence to him, several of them being drunk. His house was fired into and a child wounded and the pursued negro was also slightly wounded. The negro escaped. About 10 o'clock that night the mob returned, but failing to find the negro they then set fire to an adjacent dwelling occupied by a family of negroes in no way connected with the man and today there is a family homeless and without food or clothing, all they possessed having been destroyed by the flames started by a lawless mob. It is true, gentlemen of the grand jury, that family is composed of humble negroes, but I trust I am addressing sixteen men whose sense of justice as well as moral and physical courage are too high to allow them to consider for a moment the condition in life of any man or set of men, in the discharge of the responsible duties now devolving upon you."

This was in admirable spirit. It showed his determination to do his part as a judge to impress upon the superior white race its duties towards the inferior, helpless, weaker race. Doubtless when indictments are brought in, he will further use his power and influence from the bench to effect the punishment of the guilty persons.

This is as it should be. The white people have all the administration of the law in their hands, and they should set a high standard for themselves in their dealings with the dependent race.

It would not be surprising if some reckless stump speaker were to turn loose his vials of wrath upon Judge Alston for trying to do his duty. Possibly the fact that he is a State judge may protect him from such an assault. Furthermore, the recent one on Judge Jones has not appeared to be a profitable investment, and that may have a further deterring influence upon the disposition in some quarters to play politics wherever there is a case of white man vs. negro.

Were Dancing, When Two White Men Fired at Them-Dead and Wounded Tied Together.
WAYCROSS, Ga., Feb. 8.—Meager details of a riot, which occurred between two white men and a crowd of negroes at Beach's Still, Ga., reached this city to-day. Two negroes are said to have been killed and nine others wounded, one of them mortally. Three of the wounded were women, but their injuries are not serious. The shooting was done while a negro festival was in progress about 11 o'clock last night.

The report is that two white men well known in that section went to the festival, and after having a little difficulty with somes of the negroes, blocked the two doorways of the building in which the negroes were dancing and commenced firing into the crowd with shotguns. The men are said to have fired shot after shot into the writhing mass of humanity. The house was quickly cleared of all except some of the wounded and the men are said to have entered the building and tied the wounded and dead negroes together.

An inquest was held by the coroner over the dead bodies of the men to-day, but the verdict has not yet been announced.

Beach's still is in Coffee county, about twenty-two miles from Waycross. In this section of Coffee county several riots have occurred between the negroes and whites during the past ten years.

REIGN OF TERROR IN COFFEE.
County Thrown In Turmoll by Aaots of White Desperadoes.
County Thrown In Turmoll by Aacts of White Desperadoes.

Waycross, Ga., Feb. 11.—A terrible state of affairs exists near McDonald, in Coffee county, since the wholesale shooting of negroes by two white men last Sautrday night.

While it is known beyond quesiton who did the shooting, no arrests have been made and the negroes who saw the shooting are afraid to say anything about the affair.

The two white men are thoroughly armed and desperate, and there is no question but there will be further trouble should an attempt be made to arrest them.

Later reports from the shooting are that not less than 12 negroes were injured besides the two who were killed outright. The festival which was in progress near Beach's still Saturday is said to have been unusually peaceable until the two white men appeared without warning at each door and commenced emptying their revolvers and shotguns into the crowd.

Not less than 25 shots were fired at the negroes while a mad stampede was made for the one window. When most of the negroes had escaped the dead and some of the wounded who were left in the house were bound together by the white men. After binding the negroes the white men went through their pockets and robbed them of everything they possessed.

The white desperadoes then left the house, leaving the wounded negroes tied to the dead bodies. Returning a short time later the cords were cut and with curses and threats the negroes were informed that they would be killed if they ever told who did the shooting.

No one in that vicinity will publicly discuss the affair on account of the terror in which the desperadoes are held.

They have several friends who will undoubtedly assist them should an attempt at arrest be made.
sam-bell-waycross-1903-02-07.A22:
MURDERERS AT LARGE IN COFFEE COUNTY.
Nothing Has Been Done to Avenge Killing of Inoffensive Persons. Waveross Ga. Feb. 12. Later re-
Nothing Has Been Done to Avenge Killing of Inoffensive Persons.

Waycross, Ga., Feb. 12.—Later reports from McDonald, in Coffee county, where two negroes were killed and a number wounded by two white men last Saturday night, are to the effect that the shooting was done almost solely for the purpose of robbery. Besides the two negroes who were killed outright, not less than twelve were injured, some of them only slightly.

The dead are Sam Bell and Aleck Mervin, two turpentine hands employed at a still nearby. The negroes claim that the shooting was done by white men who reside near Beach's Still.

About 11 o'clock Saturday night, while the negro "festival" was in progress, the white men suddenly appeared at each of the two doors of the house where the festivities were going on, and without the least warning, commenced firing into the crowd. The negroes rushed for the one window of the house, and the men fired shot after shot at them, as they struggled to get out of the building. Both shot guns and revolvers were used, and not less than twenty-five shots were fired. Several of the wounded negroes were captured by the men, and after ropes were obtained, they were tied to the bodies of the two dead negroes. The white men then robbed the negroes of all the money and weapons they possessed, and left the premises. Later they returned and cut the ropes that bound the negroes, and threatened to kill them if they ever told who did the shooting.

An inquest was held over the dead bodies Sunday afternoon by a justice of the peace, but the testimony of all of them amounted to nothing.

The coroner's jury failed to obtain any information about the shooting, and returned a verdict to the effect that the negroes "came to their death by gun shot wounds from the hands of unknown parties." Sheriff Southernland was at McDonald Monday, but returned to Douglas without making any arrest.

The men are said to have been intoxicated when the shooting occurred.

It is believed that the men will not hesitate to kill any one who informs on them, and the affair is certainly kept quiet when their friends are around. An attempt will undoubtedly be made to arrest the slayers in a short time, and further trouble may be expected.

sam-bell-waycross-1903-02-07.A26:
REWARD OFFERED FOR THE MURDERERS.
Governor Wants Men Who Killed Negroes Apprehended.
Atlanta, Feb. 26.—Two cases, in which negroes were shot down without apparent cause, by unknown lawless white persons, were brought to the attention of Governor Terrell today, and the Governor offered a reward of $250 in each case, for the arrest with proof to convict, of the parties responsible for the murders.

One of the most outrageous cases is told of in the affidavit of Solicitor General John Bennett of the Brunswick Circuit. On the night of Feb. 7, a party of negroes were having a dance about two miles from McDonald's mill in Coffee county, when unknown white persons appeared at the two doors of the building and fired a fusilade upon the dancers, killing Alex Mervin and Sambo Bell, and wounding nine others, some seriously and some slightly.

After the rest of the negroes had fled in fear, the murderers entered the building, tied the bodies of the wounded to those of the dead and then robbed the dead and living of all the money they could find on their persons.

The usual reward for a person charged with murder is $150, but in this case the Governor made it $250 for each.

The other case in which similar rewards were offered was that of the murder of Will Fambro in Spalding county on the night of Feb. 23, last Monday. Fambro insulted a lady and child while intoxicated. He was arrested, pleaded guilty and was fined $40, which was paid. On Monday night, an angry mob of white men went to his home and fired a fusilade into the dwelling, killing Fambro and terrifying his wife and children.

The Governor has offered a reward of $250 for the arrest of each of the murderers.
sam-bell-waycross-1903-02-07.A29:
Lynching in Georgia.
Governor Jelks has fairly put an end to lynching in Alabama, and Governor Longino promises to do likewise in Mississippi through the punishment of the members of the cruel and cowardly mob in Attalla county. They are in jail, and bail has been refused. They must stay in jail until their trials come on, and public sentiment is distinctly against them. Every one of them may be sent to the penitentiary, although they are spending every cent they have or can command to avert such a result.

At present Georgia is the lynching state of the union, but Governor Terrell is endeavoring to break up the brutalizing practice. He is endeavoring to punish the perpetrators of two crimes in Coffee and Spalding counties. In Coffee county a mob fired into a negro dance, killing two and wounding nine others. In Spalding county another mob fired into the house of Will Fambro, a negro. Fambro had been tried for an offense, had been found guilty, had been fined, and had paid the fine. In the house were Fambro, his wife and three children, when a mob surrounded it, and he was shot to death.

Governor Terrell has offered a reward of $250 for the arrest and delivery to the authorities of each and every person connected with these mobs. But these offers of rewards will prove unavailing—they always have been powerless and wholly useless. They are simply grandstand plays. They alarm no one, and they do no good whatever. WHIPPED THE IDLE NEGROES.
Soore of Them Punished by Whites for Resenting a Beating a Teacher Received.
NEW ORLEANS, Sept. 16.—A party of whites administered severe whippings to a score of idle negroes at Sulphur Springs, Bowie county, to-day. A negro school-teacher, having made insulting remarks about a young white woman, was publicly whipped. Some of the negroes who witnessed the whipping grew indignant and denounced the outrage.

The crowd took them, also, and gave each of them a sound thrashing, warning them that unless they should go to work very quickly they would have to move out of town. There was no attempt at concealment, the negroes being publicly whipped in the streets in the presence of a large crowd.

FURIOUS Rush Made For Negro Prisoner At Hickman. OFFICERS HURRIED HIM AWAY TO STATE PRISON TO SAVE HIM FROM LYNCHING. SHOT A YOUNG WHITE MAN.
Fulton, Ky., May 15.—[Special.]—Pandemonium reigned for a time today in the Fulton Circuit Court at Hickman, and had it not been for the prompt action of Sheriff Carpenter and the court officers a lynching would surely have occurred.

Vine Bryant, a negro, was on trial for shooting Leslie Hackett, a young white man of high standing, in Hickman last fall. When placed on the stand to testify in his own behalf Bryant acknowledged he struck Hackett on the head with a pistol and as Hackett turned to get away shot him in the back. At this admission the spectators rose as one man and amid shouts of "hang him," surged forward to lay hands on the prisoner. Sheriff Carpenter jumped into the breach and held the crowd at bay while deputies rushed the negro out at a back door, hustled him into a wagon and hurriedly left town. He was driven to a point on the N., C. and St. L. railroad, where a train was boarded and the prisoner was taken to Eddyville. The jury returned a verdict of guilty without leaving their seats and the defendant was sentenced to five years in the Eddyville penitentiary.

Leslie Hackett, the victim, is still confined to his bed, suffering from a paralytic stroke which followed. The bullet entered his back, injuring the spinal column.

william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A1:
RACE RIOTING AT PITTSBURG.
One Negro Killed and Three Others Are Dying.
PITTSBURG, Pa., May 31.—As a result of a riot between negroes and whites this afternoon, one negro was shot and killed, three negroes were wounded mortally and two white men shot, but not seriously. While the riot was at its height, an attempt to lynch a negro was made. The rope was about his neck, but after a speech by a former inspector of police the mob left the negro on the ground dying.

The riot occurred in West Liberty borough, adjoining Pittsburg. The Beltzhoover Borough Baseball Club had received permission from the authorities of the borough to play ball on Sunday on condition that they kept away gamblers. When the game began five negroes were seen gambling just outside the grounds. "Sandy" Garrett, a negro constable, accompanied by some of the ball players, ordered the gamblers away. They refused to go and a fight resulted.

One of the negroes pulled a revolver and shot William Bell, a white boy, in the thigh. The crowd began to throw stones and the gamblers fled, dividing into three parties. Nelson Foster, the leader of the negroes, was caught by the crowd, pummelled until his skull was fractured and left for dead on the ground. Jack Goldmann and Burt Mayher of his crowd escaped and William Davis and Charles Kelly fled up the hill, shooting as they ran, and wounding Joseph Tumetha, a Pole, in the face.

The two gamblers took refuge in a chicken house on the farm of William Pays. "Sandy" Garrett burst the door open to arrest them. He was shot in the left lung. Although Garrett is a negro, his wounding infuriated the whites. Three ran into the farmhouse, secured a rifle and poured bullets into the coop, Kelly and Davis shooting at them through cracks in the walls. Having exhausted their ammunition, they waved a handkerchief in token of surrender.

As Kelly emerged he was shot through the heart and dropped dead. The crowd seized Davis, dragged him on his face to a tree, 300 yards away, beating him with baseball bats all the way. There was delay, because nobody could climb the tree. Former Police Inspector George Waggoner pleaded with the crowd to let Davis go. Policemen from Pittsburg arrived and dispersed the crowd. Garrett, the negro constable, William Davis and Nelson Foster are at the hospital and will die. The two whites were not dangerously wounded.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A4:
FATAL RIOT AT BALL GAME
LYNCHING NARROWLY AVERTED IN PITTSBURG.
Six Negro Crap Shooters Draw Revolvers When Ordered from the Grounds—One Beaten to Death After a Desperate Fight and Another Was Abont to be Hanged When the Mob Came to Its Senses.

Pittsburg, Pa., May 31.—In a riot at a baseball ground at High Bridge, in West Liberty borough, to-day, one negro was killed, two were probably fatally shot, a third was badly beaten and thrown over a hill and three white boys were severely but not fatally wounded. One of the negroes escaped lynching by a very narrow margin.

The dead: Charles Kelly, negro, aged thirty, literally pounded to death.

The injured: William Davis, negro, shot in the back and neck, probably fatally; Sandy Garrett, negro, shot in left breast; George Foster, negro, badly beaten with clubs and stones; Leo Merin, white boy, aged seventeen, shot in the hand; John Pierce, white, aged thirteen, shot in the groin; Joseph Tumetha, white, aged seventeen, shot in the face.

The ball ground at High Bridge is a popular resort on Sundays and to-day fully two thousand persons, men, women and boys, had congregated there to witness a game between two of the local amateur teams. Before the game had started, "Sandy" Garrett, a large negro, whom the Beltzhoover club carried as a mascot, discovered the presence of six negro crap shooters and gamblers who had come upon the ground with their paraphernalia prepared to do business. Sandy objected to this, and backed by a number of the Beltzhoover men and rooters for the club, ordered the gamblers from the grounds. The latter refused to go and produced a brace of revolvers.

The players then began to retreat and the negroes began shooting. Finding that Sandy had been partially stunned by a blow over the head, his friends rallied and with reinforcements made a rush for the gamblers. By this time probably 1,000 men and boys were in the pursuit. George Foster, one of the fugitives, was caught and terribly beaten and thrown over a hill. The two remaining fugitives continued their flight, using their revolvers freely. They took refuge in a chicken coop standing near the roadside and when Sandy made a dash for the coop, intending to drag the men out, he received a bullet in the breast under the heart and fell to the ground with a groan. Following this up, the men inside the coop would open the door, fire into the crow and then jump back to safety. One of the mob climbed to the roof and the next time the negro inside opened the door to fire, a huge rock fell and landed on his head. There was a shout of delight from the hundreds. The negro, who was identified later as Charles Kelley, fell forward, and at the same instant both arms went out and from his hands flew two revolvers. There was a rush. The man was literally pounded to death. Still thirsting for vengeance, the men rushed the coop and in a few moments, amid muffled shouts and curses, they emerged, dragging the second negro with them. Then a shout came "Get a rope; get a rope." In a few moments a stout rope was secured and with shouts of glee, it was tightened about the half nead negro and a dozen men at the other end of it started down the hill, for a distance of at lease 300 yards. The negro was bleeding from a dozen cuts and bruises and bullet wounds, and was apparently more than half dead.

Over the rough ground, the victim of the mob's fury was dragged to a large tree. Soon men were climbing the tree to fasten the rope to al imb, and it was only a question of minutes when there would have been a lynching. At this critical moment, some one yelled "Let him alone, let the law deal with him. Can't you see he's about all in." The crowd came to its senses apparently and some one else yelled, "Here comes the officers," and this settled the lynching. The negro to all appearances dead, was left lying on the ground with the rope still around his neck and the crowd walked away.

It was fully three hours later before a physician was summoned to examine the victim, who proved to be William Davis. He was later taken to a hospital in a very serious condition.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A6:
THREE ARE DEAD AS RESULT OF CRAPS
Survivor Narrowly Escapes Lynching by Angry Mob.
PITTSBURG, Pa., May 31.—Two negroes and a white boy were killed and a third negro terribly beaten in a quarrel over a game of craps at High Bridge, West Liberty, this afternoon. The enraged mob of whites had the rope about the neck of the third negro and were dragging him to a tree to lynch him when he was rescued by officers. Both sides had revolvers and during the battle a hundred or more shots were fired. The quarrel was the result of an attempt on the part of the white boys to break up the crap game and stop gambling.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A18:
Riot Leaders to Be Punished.
PITTSBURG, June 1.—An official investigation of the race riot and murder at West Liberty yesterday is being made by the county authorities. All suspicious negroes are being arrested by the South Side police and County Detective Robinson has the names of eight men, alleged to be leaders in the riot, who, he says, will be charged with murder. With the exception of the negro, Davis, who narrowly escaped lynching, all the injured are doing well. The condition of Davis is critical, and it is thought he will die.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A25:
Shot During Riot, Is Dead. DITTSBURG, June 4, "Sandy"
Shot During Riot, Is Dead.

PITTSBURG, June 4.—"Sandy" Garrett, colored, who was shot during the riot in the West Liberty borough on Sunday, died at the South Side hospital last night. William Davis, the colored man who was almost lynched by the rioters, was able to leave the hospital, and he was sent to the county jail by Coroner McGeary. Thirty-three warrants charging riot have been sworn out against supposed participants in the riot. Attorney Haymaker declares no guilty man, white or black, shall go unpunished. Four arrests have been made.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A33:
the country to-day.
That alleged Pittsburg, Pa., "raceriot" of May 31 was nothing of the kind. Two mixed (colored and white) crowds fought, the result being two dead (one white and one colored) and several (both classes) injured. The Associated Press liar got his dirty work into the daily papers of the country early, however.

The sentencing to ten years' imprisonment in the Missouri penitentiary of a white brute by the name of Samuel Mitchell, who led the Joplin mob that lynched an Afro-American by the name of Thomas Gilyard some weeks ago, is very encouraging indeed. We sincerely trust that the pardon officials of that state will permit him to serve the term.

The recent Alabama decision of the United States supreme court has not discouraged Virginia and Alabama Afro-Americans who have been fighting disfranchisement in the courts. It has only encouraged them to continue the fight with renewed vigor and on broader grounds. Our people all over the country should contribute liberally and assist them in compliance with their appeals. Their fight is our fight—the Afro-American's.

A pamphlet containing two exceptionally strong articles, "Why The Negro Was Enfranchised," and "Negro Suffrage Justified," by Mr. R. E. Hallowell, of Boston, Mass., assisted by Butler R. Wilson, esq., of the same city, has been received by The Gazette, and is the best and most timely publication we have seen. Too many copies could not be published nor can too many like it be issued. A more general distribution for it and all that follow, should be provided for. For instance, at least two copies should be sent to every daily newspaper in the north particularly, and to as many individuals of all classes, as it is possible to reach. Every race newspaper ought to publish the articles the pamphlet contains and every intelligent Afro-American, north and south, should be in possession of one or more copies.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A34:
Our Blind Neighbors.
Selma Times.
Selma Times.

One negro was killed, two other negroes were seriously wounded and two white boys badly hurt in a riot recently. Some negroes opened a "crap" game at a baseball match and refused to close it when ordered by the police. A fight followed in which the crowd took part, and many shots were fired. One of the negro gamblers was shot dead and another pounded with baseball bats and stones till he all but died. He would have been hanged to a tree only for the intervention of a pitying prize fighter. All this did not happen in the South, but at West Liberty, a suburb of the city of Pittsburg, in the State of Pennsylvania. Now, if it had taken place in the South Dr. Hillis, Dr. Roosevelt and a score of other learned gentlemen up North with D. D's., LL. D's., M. D', etc., would have arisen and preached about how the poor, downtrodden negro is murdered and beaten in the South. But as it occurred in Pennsylvania they will forget to preach about it.
william-davis-west-liberty-1903-05-31.A38:
Lounger's Column.
One of the contributing causes to the race problem is a partial enforcement of the laws against miscegenation. The villages and small towns throughout the south are rocking cesspools of intimorality, and the colored women are the victims of a lustful crew of white men. The law is adequate to protect the humblest Negro and his family if there were men in authority with sufficient moral courage to enforce it. We are told by democratic politicians that the Negro is naturally inferior to the white people, and that because of this natural superiority the whites and the blacks will not mix, yet the faces of the black population belle the statement and show that there is a terrible mixing going on. The Negro is no fool. He is aware that he is being taken advantage of, and now and then, as in the Pittsburg riot, he resents the wrong. That terrible trouble all arose over a white man being caught with a colored woman in a community of respectable people, and they sought to punish him for his boldness, but because of the clanishness of the whites they did not seek the truth of the matter, but took up the hue and cry of a "Nigger" mobbing a white man, and the whole community wont wild and even to this day, have never told the world the main cause of that trouble. Either abolish the law on miscegenation or enforce it. The black man can live under law impartially enforced.

There is no reason why he couldn't raise a respectable family with laws against miscegenation. If there is a natural gulf between the races, and because of it they won't mix; the law is superfluous any way, but since we have it let us have it enforced. If Negroes know of any violation of this law going on, turn both parties up. If the police will not make the arrest, go before the grand jury of your country and produce your evidence and put the onus of the violations of the law upon those who should bear it. If you are going to live here let us protect our women and children. Try the law first, let us be law-abiding, but protect your women against the lustful of any race at any cost.

william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A1:
LYNCHING PARTY IN OHIO.
Looking for a Negro Who Confessed to Murder.
Kenton, Ohio. Aug. 1.—Harry Minard, sixty years old, was found dead with a bullet hole in his breast at his home, three miles from here, early to-day. William Nickolson, a negro, is suspected of the crime. According to Nickolson's sister, he confessed to her that he had killed Minard and took $200 in money.

He has fled from town. A posse is in pursuit, and there are threats that if captured he will be lynched.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A6:
DEAD BODY FOUND
Bill NichOls, a Colored Man. is Charged With the Murder.
Tuesday, Mr. A. Minor and Bill Nichols, a colored man who worked for him, went from the home near McGuffey, in Hardin county to work in the onion fields of the marshes.

Tuesday the colored man showed $136 and a watch to his sister and nephew and gave her $2.00 to drive him to Roundhead. He told her he had won the money in a poker game and had killed the man in a quarrel.

Thursday, the neighbors becoming suspicious formed a party to look for the missing man, and were rewarded Saturday when two men found the body under a tree near the Erle railroad about one mile west of McGuffey.

The body was in a terrlble condition, a bullet hole was in his right cheek but the bulet could not be traced.

The Hardin County commissioners have offered $100 for the capture of Nichols.

Relatives say he shot a man about 20 years ago, and he told his sister he wanted to kill one more man and then he would be ready to go straight to h-1.

Minor's body was buried, Saturday. No relatives of the murdered man appeared.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A10:
THREATS, BUT NO LYNCHING.
Crowd at Kenton, O., Does Not Molest Negro Accused of Murder.
KENTON, O., Aug. 4.—William Nichols, colored, accused of the murder of Alpha Minard, near McGuffey, and for whom search has been going on for several days, is in jail here. He was arrested at Carmel by Sheriff Griffith, of Hardin county. A crowd awaited the train on its arrival here, and many angry threats were made, but the sheriff got his prisoner to the jail without trouble. Nichols denies his guilt.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A11:
OHIO CROWDS THREATEN NEGRO.
Kenton, Ohio, Aug. 4—William Nichols, colored, accused of the murder of Alpha Minard, near McGuffey, and for whom search has been going on for two weeks, is locked up in the jail here. He was arrested at Carmel by Sheriff Griffith, of Hardin County. When the train which was bringing the prisoner to this city reached Belle Centre about two hundred residents of the vicinity where Minard had lived were gathered at the station. Nichols was observed in the car, and immediately cries of "Shoot him"" and "Hang him"" were set up by the crowd. Fearing mob violence the train quickly pulled cut.

Another crowd awaited the train on its arrival here, and many angry threats were made, but the Sheriff got his prisoner to the jail without trouble. Nichols denies his guilt, but, during the few hours he has been locked up he has made many conflicting statements.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A17:
MOB ALL ALONG THE LINE
Officers Run the Gantlet in Ohio—Lynch ing Brewing Out in Idaho State.
Kenton, O., Aug. 5.—Wm. Nichols, colored, accused of the murder of Alpha Minard, near McGuffey, and for whom search has been going on for several days, is locked up in the jail here. He was arrested in Hardin county, and en route here a mob threatened the train at Belle Center, and another when it reached here. The officers were equal to the occasion, however.

Lewiston, Ida., Aug. 5. — William Hamilton, aged 25 years, confessed to the murder and mutilation of Mabel Richards, an 11-year-old girl whose body was found near Anatone. The child was waylaid by Hamilton while en route to Sunday school. Hamilton is in jail at Asotin. In all probability he will be lynched.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A20:
WOULD LYNCH NEGRO.
Ohio Negro Dodges the Rope and Is Safe in Jail.
Kenton, O., Aug. 6.—William Nichols, colored, accused of the murder of Alpha Minard, near McGuffey, and for whom search has been going on for two weeks, is locked up in the jail here.

He was arrested at Carmel by Sheriff Griffith, of Hardin county. When the train which was bringing the prisoner to this city reached Belle Center a crowd of about 200 residents of the vicinity where Minard lived was gathered at the depot. Nichols was observed in the car, and immediately cries of "Shoot him and "Hang him" were set up by the crowd. Fearing mob violence the train quickly pulled out.

Another crowd awaited the train on its arrival here, and many angry threats were made, but the sheriff got his prisoner to the jail without trouble.

Nichols denies his guilt, but during the few hours he has been locked up he has made many conflicting statements.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A21: Nichols, who is charged with the murder of Minor, near McGuffey, Hardin county. blames the murder on his two nephews, Harl Nichols and Claudius Gibson. If he knew this, why did he not inform on them at the time? If they were connected with it, it was probably at his instigation. Minor was from Bowling Green, and a sister has come to Kenton to claim the body.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A22: William Nichols, colored (nearly white), was indicted for murder in the first degree by the Grand Jury in Kenton last week. It will be remembered Nichols was in jail for the alleged killing of A. Minard, near McGuffey some months ago.
william-nichols-belle-centre-1903-08-04.A26:
Aged Murderer
Gives His Life

In Return For Murder of His Friend of His Friend.

AN ATHEIST
He So Professed Himself to Be.
Created No Scene as He Walked to the Death Chair.--Body Goes to Medical College.
William Nichols, 68, Hardin county, was electrocuted Thursday night in the annex of the Ohio penitentiary for the murder of Alfred Minard, near Kenton, July 28, 1903.

Nichols' body was taken from the chair to the deadhouse of the penitentiary, and will be turned over to a medical college, no relatives claiming it.

Warden Gould entered the annex where Nichols was confined to read him the death warrant. He insisted upon hearing it read, and afterward made but one request, that he be given some whisky before he entered the death chamber, "just to strengthen the nerves," as he said.

He refused several times to have Chaplain Starr pray with him, preferring to die a professed Atheist. He expressed fear that his body would be turned over to a medical college, but seemed at the same time to believe that his brother, who resides at Cynthiana, Ky., would not see this happen. He did not know that the money found upon his person after he had killed and robbed Alfred Minard had been turned over some time ago to Minard's relatives, but expressed the belief that it would be sufficient to bury him.

When Nichols was received at the Ohio penitentiary one year ago last month, he stated that he was 67 years of age. Nichols was a mulatto, and could neither read nor write. He served in the Union army, his victim being a civil war veteran.

Nichols made no demonstration when placed in the chair. He came forward coolly. When the death warrant were adjusted he complained that one strap hurt his arm. "You're hurting my arm," he said: "I tell you, you are hurting my arm." When asked if he had anything to say, he never spoke, merely shook his head. At 12:04 the current was turned on. At 12:11 the physicians pronounced him dead.

In the confession Nichols recently made he said:

"Minard and I lived together about 40 days in the marshes near Kenton. He had some money, about $100, and we gambled for it and I won it. On July 28, 1903, we were pretty drunk, and went to Alger, a small town near Kenton, and drank some more.

"On the way back to the cabin we came to the forks of the road, one leading to McGuffey, another small town, and Minard wanted to go there and get more liquor, but I dissented. Finally we sat down under a tree and began to gamble.

ENGAGED IN QUARREL.

"He had no money but put up a gold watch against a $10 bill, and I won the watch. We got into a quarrel, and he struck me on the left arm with a club, and then pulled a gun. He shot at me twice, one bullet going through my left shirt sleeve. In self-derense I hit him in the head with a stone and then shot at him, the second shot killing him. I left him lying there and never saw the body again."

The country north of Bellecenter is infested with a gang of holdup men that have been getting in their work pretty regularly. Within the past three weeks three roberies have been committed, the victims in each case being relieved of small amounts of money, the largest amount being $27 and a watch. The last case reported was by the son of Robert Sloan, who was a victim of the gang one night last week.

It is reported that a Bellecenter young man was ordered to stop on the road near Yelverton Sunday night, but instead he applied the whip to his horse and escaped. — Bellecenter Herald.

A. H. Hayward, general superintendent of the Dayton, Springfield and Urbana Traction company, one of the Appleyard lines, Thursday resigned his position with the company to accept the position of general manager of the York Traction company of York, Pa., at a handsome increase in salary. The resignation is effective upon the appointment of his successor. His headquarters are at Springfield.

There was a meeting of the W. C. T. U. held in the lecture room of the First Baptist church Thursday afternoon. Rev. J. M. Faris delivered an interesting address, the subject of which was "Sabbath Observance."

Thomas W. Lawson's advertising campaign against amalgamated copper caused a sensational price decline in New York on Thursday.
